en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its nearly perfect cone shape.
The Philippine eagle is a rare bird of prey endemic to the tropical forests of Mindanao.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through the Cagayan Valley.
Lake Taal in Batangas is a freshwater lake situated inside a large volcanic caldera.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest peak in the Philippines, standing at 2,954 meters.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical grass-covered mounds that turn brown during summer.
The Tubbataha Reef in the Sulu Sea is a protected marine sanctuary famous for its rich coral biodiversity.
Palawan is the largest island in the Mimaropa region and is known for its extensive limestone caves.
Baguio City experiences a subtropical highland climate, making it significantly cooler than the rest of the Philippines.
The Philex mine in Benguet is one of the largest copper and gold mining operations in the Philippines.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features an eight-kilometer navigable underground river flowing directly into the sea.
The San Bernardino Strait separates the Bicol Region from Eastern Visayas and connects the Philippine Sea to the Sibuyan Sea.
